display.title: Every Step Is Perfectly Planned: The Innkeeper and the Mice
display.summary_short: Everything Hashem creates has a purpose: an innkeeper falsely accused by a drunken neighbor is told by the Tzemach Tzedek that even mice can help a Jew.
display.summary_long: After the song 'I Believe in Hashem', the storyteller explains that everything in the world follows Hashem's perfect plan, except our free choice in Torah and mitzvos, so we need not worry. From this week's Parshas Shemos he shows the power of bitachon: Moshe Rabbeinu feared that his deed was known, and the Midrash says that because he feared, Pharaoh heard. The Tzemach Tzedek taught, 'Think good and it will be good.' The story follows Hilke, an honest Jewish innkeeper loved by his customers, except for Stepan, a drunken Jew-hater who is refused drinks on credit. For revenge, Stepan and four crooked witnesses falsely report that Hilke sells untaxed vodka. Hilke's wife, the daughter of a Lubavitcher Chassid, convinces him to go to the Tzemach Tzedek, who tells him to strengthen his bitachon and adds that everything Hashem created has a purpose, even mice. At the trial Stepan contradicts himself, none of his witnesses can come, and the signed police report turns out to have been eaten by mice, while every other drawer is untouched. The case is dismissed. The storyteller closes with the Rebbe's promise that Moshiach is coming, and Torah, tefillah and tzedakah for the Hakhel year.
display.lesson: Everything Hashem creates has a purpose and every step is planned for our good, so trust Hashem, think good, and rely on the words of a tzaddik.
